title: lore link's tracker write is a read-modify-write with no --if-revision, so a concurrent change to documentation is silently clobbered
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-17 against the installed quest 0.7.1, not inferred from help text. Prompted by a quest-cli note about their own whole-list-rewrite hazard (QCLI-323); they asked whether lore drives "quest task edit" programmatically anywhere. It does, and it is exposed.

THE EXPOSURE. src/adapters/quest.ts:444-451 builds "quest task edit" and forwards patch.doc as repeated --doc flags. Labels are incremental and safe (--add-label / --remove-label). documentation is NOT: --doc has no --add-doc / --remove-doc counterpart, and it REPLACES the whole list.

Both lore call sites therefore do a read-modify-write with no precondition:
  - src/commands/link.ts:294-295  const desiredDocs = addDoc(detail.documentation, docPath); await adapter.editTask(taskId, { addLabels: [label], doc: desiredDocs })
  - src/commands/link.ts:468      await adapter.editTask(taskId, { removeLabels: [label], doc: removeDoc(detail.documentation, docPath) })

Each reads the task's current documentation, computes a new whole list, and writes it back. Anything that changed documentation between the read and the write is silently discarded. Classic lost update. Nothing in lore passes --if-revision.

MEASUREMENT 1 -- --doc REPLACES. Scratch workspace, real quest 0.7.1:
  quest task create "probe" --doc a.md --doc b.md   -> documentation ["a.md","b.md"]
  quest task edit T-1 --doc a.md                    -> documentation ["a.md"]
b.md was dropped with no warning and exit 0.

MEASUREMENT 2 -- --if-revision REFUSES A STALE WRITE (the remedy's rejecting half). Captured revision from task view --json, let a second writer touch the record, then wrote with the stale revision:
  exit 5, {"error_type":"conflict","message":"Task state changed concurrently; the operation was not applied.","hint":"Read the latest task state and retry the operation.","input":{"actualRevision":"1bc08bc0..."}}
It names the actual current revision, so a caller can re-read and retry without guessing.

MEASUREMENT 3 -- --if-revision ACCEPTS A CURRENT WRITE (the accepting half, measured separately because neither half implies the other): same edit with the freshly-read revision returned exit 0 and applied. Without this half, an always-refusing precondition would look like a working guard.

WHY THIS IS REACHABLE HERE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL. This fleet routinely runs several agents against one tracker concurrently, each in its own worktree, and .quest is committed so a merge can also move a record between a read and a write. lore link is exactly the command that writes tracker back-references for docs.

THE FIX, and it is small: capture `revision` from the task read that already happens, thread it through EditTaskPatch, and pass --if-revision on any patch that includes a whole-list field. On exit 5, re-read and retry with a bounded retry -- Quest never retries a write conflict for the caller, by design, and its refusal already carries actualRevision. Quest's own contract calls the precondition optional and behavior unchanged when omitted, so this is additive.

SCOPE QUESTION TO DECIDE, not assume: whether --if-revision should be passed on EVERY editTask or only on patches carrying a replacement-semantics field. Passing it always is simpler to reason about and turns any concurrent movement into a retry; passing it selectively avoids spurious conflicts on purely incremental label edits. Check the other adapters too -- src/adapters/backlog.ts:1041 and src/adapters/jira.ts:328 implement the same editTask interface and may have their own version of this.

RELATED, SAME FUNCTION, DIFFERENT DEFECT: LCLI-495 is about runLink writing the Story's tasks: frontmatter BEFORE the tracker back-reference can refuse, leaving the link half-applied. This task is about the tracker write itself silently clobbering a concurrent change. Whoever picks up LCLI-495 is already in this code and should consider doing both -- but they are genuinely separate failures and either fix leaves the other standing.

ACCEPTANCE SHAPE: a lore link (or unlink) whose target task was modified by another writer between lore's read and its write must NOT silently discard that modification -- proven by a test that interleaves a concurrent edit, and mutation-checked by removing the precondition and confirming the test goes red.
implementationNotes: DEDUPE PASS 2026-09-17 (OPAG-176): related to, not a duplicate of, LCLI-495. Both are lore-link tracker-write-safety defects in the same file (src/commands/link.ts), but different failure modes -- this task is about a missing --if-revision precondition on a read-modify-write, LCLI-495 is about write-ORDERING (Story frontmatter written before the tracker back-reference can refuse). Left as two records deliberately; each is independently actionable.
finalSummary: Fixed and delivered in PR #179 (merged to dev as 0325675d). CLOSED LATE, IN THE FOLLOWING PR, AND THAT IS A DEFECT OF MINE TO RECORD RATHER THAN HIDE: this task merged still marked In Progress with no final summary. It was not a deliberate deferral under the post-merge-evidence carve-out -- the closing evidence (PR number and CI run id) was available before the merge, so the rule applied in full. What broke my sequence: I had accidentally committed this task's implementation onto local dev instead of its feature branch, and the repair work displaced the close. Recorded here because 'closed in the next PR' and 'deferred for post-merge evidence' look identical in a record, and only one of them is legitimate. This was the other one. DEFECT: lore link/unlink perform a read-modify-write on tracker labels -- read the task's current labels, decide which to remove, then write. A competing writer landing between the read and the write made that decision stale and the write applied ANYWAY, silently clobbering a change lore never saw. Found by opum-cli-e2e while reviewing the seam for the quest 0.9.0 pair. FIX: Quest has carried the precondition since QCLI-277 (--if-revision <revision>, refused with an exit-5 conflict naming the record's actual current revision) and lore was simply not using it; task view --json already returns revision and the adapter dropped it. The revision now flows from the read that made the decision into the write that acts on it. DETECTED BY PRESENCE, NEVER BY A VERSION COMPARISON, and this is the part that could have gone badly: passing the flag unconditionally would have raised lore's effective Quest floor from MIN_QUEST_VERSION (0.2.7) to whichever release added it, breaking every Quest in between -- an external compatibility change wearing the costume of a bug fix, and one that would have quietly reversed a product-owner decision recorded in the adapter's own comment (an exact-match allowlist was deliberately replaced by a floor because lore and Quest release independently). The adapter reads the manifest it already fetches during probe and asks whether task edit advertises the flag. A test pins the omission path against a stub reporting 0.7.1 -- the very version that DOES support it -- so a version-based implementation fails that test rather than passing by luck. THE RETRY IS NOT OPTIONAL: adding the precondition alone would have traded a silent clobber for a user-visible failure on a link that used to succeed, which is more correct and less useful. withConflictRetry re-runs the whole read-decide-write cycle so a retry re-reads and re-decides rather than re-issuing a stale patch; bounded at three, because a conflict means a competing writer won and retrying is only worth it while contention is incidental. Quest's own agent contract states it does not retry write conflicts and the caller should perform a bounded retry -- this is the caller half of that contract. ifRevision and revision are both OPTIONAL on the shared tracker types, so Backlog and Jira ignore them and their behaviour is unchanged. MUTATION-TESTED, red sets predicted from the test files BEFORE running: detection forced true reddens only the omission test; forced false, only the pass-through test; removing the retry reddens the convergence test; widening the bound from 3 to 5 reddens ONLY the bound test (87 pass, 1 fail). That last one is the useful measurement -- the bound is genuinely independent of convergence rather than the same property asserted twice, and it is the test that matters most because without the bound it would not fail, it would HANG. EVIDENCE: CI run 35407787285 on head 6c42a279, CI pull_request, completed/success. Full suite 3311 pass / 0 fail; typecheck and lint exit 0. NOTE ON THE PAIR: quest 0.9.0 flips nine removal flags to exit 6 on a miss. That release does NOT create this race -- it removes the silence that hid it. opum-cli-e2e's TASK-90 exercises the seam under concurrency and, because this landed first, states itself as a regression guard on a landed fix rather than as a defect probe.
